writingStyle.description: Language quality guidance injected into all LLM prompts
writingStyle.titles: 3-6 words. Plain noun phrase that names the specific error. No parentheticals or clarifications inside parentheses. Write the error directly: 'Did Not Flip the Second Fraction' — never 'Did Not Flip the Second Fraction (no reciprocal)'.
writingStyle.descriptions: 2-3 sentences maximum. Keep it concrete and specific. Do NOT start every sentence with 'Students' — vary the subject. Good openers: the error itself ('Slope and intercept get swapped...'), a conditional ('When reading y = mx + b, the two numbers...'), or the consequence ('The result is...'). One idea per sentence. No hedging words (often, typically, usually, tend to). Do not restate the same idea in different words. Write for a classroom teacher, not a researcher.
writingStyle.instructionalMoves: Write in short, scannable chunks. Use plain conversational language — imagine a teacher reading this quickly between classes. Break steps into separate sentences. Avoid dense paragraphs. No academic or clinical language. Active voice. Each instruction should be one action: 'Show students two worked examples side by side.' not 'Teachers should consider presenting students with two worked examples simultaneously for comparison purposes.'
writingStyle.successIndicators: Start each with an action verb. Describe observable student behavior only. 10 words max per indicator.

genMisconception.description: microcoachv2LLMGenMisconception — extracts the misconceptions behind a PPQ's wrong answer options from the question stems, option content and response counts. New documents carry no Distractors column, so this mapping is generated rather than read. Output is recorded for review; not yet consumed downstream.
styleExamples: Added exponents when multiplying powers with different bases
Reported the median as the middle of the unsorted list
Applied the negative sign to only the first term in the parentheses
Read the 3 in y = 3x as the starting value instead of the rate
genMisconception.styleExamplesNote: Register only, for the per-option `text` field. Deliberately off-domain: these were in-domain teacher notes from the pilot Algebra document until 2026-09-16, and that document is the same assessment the fixtures use, so in-domain examples risk being copied onto the very questions being analysed. Each names a reasoning step that determines a specific wrong value — the property the prompt's part (a) asks for — rather than a bare slip.
genMisconception.enforceAdmissionNote: true makes validateOutput's well-formedness checks act rather than just report. The remedy matches the level of the fault: a bad option explanation drops that reference only (like `unknownRef` and `markedCorrect` already do), and a misconception left with no references then falls to `noValidRefs`; a disjunctive title drops the whole misconception, because no edit to its option list would fix it. Every hit is listed in `admissionFlags` whether or not it caused a drop, so nothing is silent. Enabled 2026-10-03; the level split came after two runs where a whole-misconception drop cost more than the fault did (v22 lost "Took coefficient as slope", v23 lost "Incorrect substitution for y"). Watch `admissionFlags` each eval: losing something from the stable clusters means a rule is wrong, not the model.
